@elonmusk Conclusion: Dogecoin isn’t bulletproof. Mining, inflation, whale wallets, hype, regulation, all real risks. But compared to every other meme, it’s still the only one with decentralisation in its DNA. That gives $DOGE the highest survival odds. 🐕🚀 Penke🥸

@elonmusk RISK 6: Every cycle, new memecoins launch. $Pepe, $Shiba, $BONK. They pump, then fade. Dogecoin has the first-mover edge, but it’s always fighting for attention in the meme arena. And people want gains. They pump coins that not pumped yet. So they can sell on the hype they are
@elonmusk RISK 5: Regulators haven’t decided what Dogecoin even is. Commodity? Security? Meme exception? A crackdown on trading venues could hit liquidity fast.
RISK 4: $DOGE lives and dies by memes. @elonmusk  tweets → price moves. Great for spikes, dangerous for long-term stability. A coin shouldn’t need a mascot to survive.
RISK 3: A handful of wallets hold a big chunk of supply. Some are exchanges, some are whales. That means influence isn’t perfectly spread, even after 10 years of distribution $DOGE.
RISK 2: Dogecoin has no hard cap. 10,000 new DOGE are minted every minute. If demand slows down, that inflation dilutes value. Supply pressure never stops.

Still, $DOGE isn’t risk-free. 

RISK 1: Mining is merged with Litecoin. That’s good for security, but it also concentrates hashpower in a few pools. Too much reliance on too few players.

Dogecoin launched fair in 2013. No premine. No central treasury. Secured by merged mining with Litecoin. Distributed through years of mining and tipping. Not perfect decentralisation, but miles ahead of every other meme. That’s why $DOGE survives, in my opinion. 😆
Dogecoin isn’t Bitcoin-level decentralised, but it’s the only memecoin that even comes close. In my opinion that’s enough to give $DOGE real survivability while the rest fade out. 🐕🚀 #PenkeTrading
